result.summary: Revised the single evidence file per the follow-up requirements, replacing the prior full-buffer decoder with a row-scoped `_decode_row(bytes, row)` that validates the row index against CONSTRUCTION_CAPACITY, checks total observed length against independently measured (var_to_bytes-derived, no header/offset guesses) per-segment lengths, verifies each segment's Variant type and count, extracts only that row's scalar(s) via `_extract_scalar()`, and lets each decoded packed array fall out of scope immediately after — no 18-segment dictionary is retained. Added a single documented `_expected_retired_row(type_id, phase, refund_policy)` helper covering all 16 row fields (using Construction's own public PURPOSE_BUILD/MAX_BUILDERS/PHASE_*/REFUND_* constants and EntityDirectory.NULL_SLOT/NULL_GENERATION rather than duplicated magic numbers), applied identically across all three histories; each test now asserts all 16 retained fields plus the 4 delivered-material cells and live_count for every history (previously only 6 fields were checked on the two stockpile cases). Building type ids 6 (dirt_path) and 19 (open_stockpile) are frozen local constants, each cross-checked against a live `Catalog.BUILDING_DEFINITION` lookup with its own assertion rather than being derived solely from the catalog at test time. Every setup step now goes through a `_require(ok, message) -> bool` helper that asserts and lets the test method return early and safely on any failed op or failed decode, before any dictionary indexing occurs. The corruption-witness test now decodes at row 0 explicitly and asserts the refusal's error is the named `TOTAL_LENGTH_MISMATCH` code for both the truncated and the appended-byte cases, not just a generic falsy `ok`. No production files, extra API surface, or new persisted format were touched; the focus runner is unchanged and not included in this bundle. No execution was performed or claimed here.
